docs.title: vexy-vid
docs.text: vexy-vid is a command-line tool that crops, trims and rescales video files. It can find letterbox bars and the subtitle band on its own, and it encodes the result with a hardware encoder when your ffmpeg build has one.

docs.title: What goes in, what comes out
docs.text:
You give vexy-vid one video file and a description of the frame you want. It builds an ffmpeg filter chain (crop, optionally followed by scale), re-encodes the video stream, copies the audio stream unchanged, and writes a new file next to the original.

vexy-vid trim --Letterbox --input movie.mp4

For a 640×480 clip with 64-pixel black bars at the top and bottom, this command:

  1. Runs ffmpeg's cropdetect filter over the first 60 seconds.
  2. Reads the detected content area, 640x352 at offset (0,64).
  3. Removes 64 pixels from the top and 64 pixels from the bottom.
  4. Writes movie_trim_llb.mp4, a 640×352 video.

docs.title: Two commands
docs.text:
Command Use it to Example crop Keep a window of a given size and discard the rest vexy-vid crop --crop 16:9 --input video.mp4 trim Remove a number of pixels or a percentage from each edge vexy-vid trim --top 100 --bottom 50 --input video.mp4

Both commands accept --scale to resize the result in the same pass, and --quality to choose between fast and high-quality encoding.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Crop to exact pixels (1280x720), an aspect ratio (16:9) or a percentage (50%x50%), with --Halign and --Valign to place the crop window.
  • Trim edges like reversed CSS padding: --top, --right, --bottom, --left.
  • Detect letterbox bars with ffmpeg cropdetect, with an OpenCV fallback.
  • Detect the subtitle band at the bottom of the frame and trim it away.
  • Encode with NVIDIA NVENC, Intel Quick Sync or AMD AMF when ffmpeg supports them, and fall back to libx265 or libx264 when it does not.
  • Cache detection results so a second run on the same file skips the analysis.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer.
  • The ffmpeg binary on your PATH. It is a system program, not a Python package. See Installation.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: vexy-vid is a small Python package in src/vexy_vid/. The command-line interface is a thin layer over two functions, crop() and trim(). Each one measures the input, builds an ffmpeg filter string and hands it to the encoder.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
vexy-vid trim --Letterbox -i movie.mp4
        │
        ▼
cli.main()            fire.Fire({"crop": crop, "trim": trim})
        │
        ▼
trim.trim()           get_input_path() → get_video_info()  (ffprobe: 640x480)
        │             detect_letterbox_ffmpeg()             (top=64, bottom=64)
        │             validate_crop_parameters()
        │             generate_output_path()                (movie_trim_llb.mp4)
        ▼
video filter          "crop=640:352:0:64"
        │
        ▼
encoder.process_video_with_hardware_encoding()
                      HardwareEncoderDetector.get_best_encoder()  (libx265)
                      ffmpeg -i movie.mp4 -vf crop=640:352:0:64 -c:v libx265 -acodec copy ...

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Module Contents cli.py main(), the console entry point. Configures loguru and exposes crop and trim through Fire. crop.py crop(): computes the window size and offset and builds crop=W:H:X:Y, optionally followed by scale=W:H. trim.py trim(): runs detection, combines detected and manual trims, validates the result and builds the filter. utils.py parse_size(), parse_dimension(), get_video_info(), get_input_path(), generate_output_path(), validate_crop_parameters() and the VideoAnalysisCache class. analysis.py detect_letterbox_ffmpeg(), detect_letterbox_opencv_parallel(), detect_subtitles_morphological_parallel(), detect_subtitles_brightness_fast(), and the Numba-compiled pixel loops. frames.py extract_frame_fast(): decodes one frame with PyAV, with an ffmpeg command-line fallback. pipeline.py VideoProcessingPipeline (a reader thread and up to four worker threads) and FrameBufferPool. encoder.py HardwareEncoderDetector and process_video_with_hardware_encoding(). constants.py Detection thresholds, pool and queue sizes, and the encoder priority lists.

docs.title: Frame analysis pipeline
docs.text:
The OpenCV letterbox fallback and the subtitle shape analysis use VideoProcessingPipeline.process_frames_parallel():

  1. A reader thread calls extract_frame_fast() for each requested frame index and puts (index, frame) pairs on an input queue.
  2. Up to four worker threads take frames from the queue, run the analysis function on each, and put (index, result) pairs on an output queue.
  3. When the reader finishes, it puts one None sentinel on the input queue. Each worker that receives it puts it back before exiting, so every worker sees it.
  4. The collector gathers results until every worker has signalled the end, then returns the results in the original frame order. Frames that failed give None.

The per-pixel loops (calculate_row_luminance, find_black_borders, count_bright_pixels_per_row) are compiled with Numba's @jit(nopython=True). Two of them use parallel=True to spread rows across CPU cores.

docs.title: Using vexy-vid from Python
docs.text:
The command functions are plain Python functions. Their keyword arguments match the command-line flags:

from vexy_vid.crop import crop
from vexy_vid.trim import trim

crop(input="movie.mp4", crop="16:9", Valign=100)
trim(input="movie.mp4", Letterbox=True, output="movie-clean.mp4")

Both functions return None, write the output file, and raise an exception on failure.

The size parser is useful on its own:

from vexy_vid.utils import parse_size

parse_size("16:9", 1440, 1080)      # (1440, 810)
parse_size("50%x720", 1920, 1080)   # (960, 720)

The installed version is available as vexy_vid.__version__:

import vexy_vid
print(vexy_vid.__version__)

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
• ffmpeg filters go in through the output stage. The crop and scale chain is passed to ffmpeg-python as the vf output option, and global flags such as -loglevel are attached with .global_args().
  • cropdetect needs info logging. The detector captures ffmpeg's standard error and runs at -loglevel info (or verbose with --verbose), because cropdetect prints its results at that level.
  • Import order. av is imported before cv2. Both bundle their own libavdevice on macOS; see Troubleshooting.
  • Capitalised parameters. Halign, Valign and Letterbox keep their capital letters because Fire uses parameter names as flag names. Renaming them would change the command-line interface.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: This page mirrors CHANGELOG.md in the repository. The project uses git-tag-driven semantic versioning through hatch-vcs.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Encoding was broken against current ffmpeg-python. encoder.py called stream.video.filter_complex(...), which does not exist in the installed ffmpeg-python, so every crop/trim encode raised AttributeError. The crop/scale chain is now passed through as the -vf output option.
  • ffmpeg.run(global_args=...) is not a valid keyword in the installed ffmpeg-python and raised TypeError. Global flags (-loglevel) are now attached to the stream via .global_args(...).
  • Letterbox auto-detection always found nothing in the default mode. detect_letterbox_ffmpeg ran ffmpeg at -loglevel error, but cropdetect prints its crop= result at info level — so the parser saw an empty log whenever --verbose was off. Detection now runs at info (captured internally, never shown to the user).
  • The parallel frame pipeline deadlocked. The reader emitted a single None sentinel while up to four processor workers consumed the queue, so three workers looped forever and the collector hung. Each worker now re-posts the sentinel before exiting, so it propagates to every worker. This affected trim --subtitles and the OpenCV letterbox fallback.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Test suite (tests/, 48 tests): unit tests for size/dimension parsing, output-path generation, crop validation, the Numba detection kernels, the OpenCV frame processors, and encoder config selection; ffmpeg-gated integration tests that generate a synthetic letterboxed clip and exercise crop, trim (explicit + --Letterbox), frame extraction, and the parallel pipeline end to end.
  • .github/workflows/ci.yml — lint, format check, and tests on Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 with ffmpeg installed.
  • .github/workflows/release.yml — build and PyPI trusted publishing plus a GitHub release on v* tags.
  • Jekyll documentation under docs/ (home, usage, hardware acceleration) using the Just the Docs remote theme, plus a project icon at docs/assets/icon.png.
  • pytest/coverage configuration, pytest-cov dev dependency, CLAUDE.md, PLAN.md, DEPENDENCIES.md.

docs.title: [1.0.4] and earlier
docs.text: Initial package: crop and trim commands, PyAV frame extraction, Numba pixel analysis, hardware-encoder detection, hatch-vcs packaging.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
vexy-vid has two commands, crop and trim. Both read one video, write one video, and accept --scale to resize the result.

vexy-vid COMMAND [FLAGS]

The command-line interface is generated by Python Fire from the crop() and trim() function signatures. Run vexy-vid crop --help or vexy-vid trim --help to see the flags your installed version accepts.

Capitalised flags

--Halign, --Valign and --Letterbox start with a capital letter. Fire turns each Python parameter name into a flag of the same spelling, so --letterbox (lower case) is not recognised.

docs.title: crop
docs.text:
Keep a window of a given size and discard the rest.

vexy-vid crop --crop SIZE [--scale SIZE] [--Halign N] [--Valign N] --input FILE
Flag Short Default Meaning --input -i standard input Input video path. When missing, one line is read from standard input. --output -o generated Output video path. See Output file names. --crop -c full frame Size of the window to keep, in any size format. --scale -s none Size to scale to after cropping. Percentages refer to the cropped size. --Halign -H 50 Horizontal window position: 0 left, 50 centre, 100 right. --Valign -V 50 Vertical window position: 0 top, 50 centre, 100 bottom. --quality -q 1 0 fast, 1 balanced, 2 quality. See Hardware acceleration. --verbose -v False Show debug logs and ffmpeg's info output.

docs.title: How the window is placed
docs.text:
crop computes the window size from --crop, then places it with the alignment values:

  • x = (original width − window width) × Halign / 100
  • y = (original height − window height) × Valign / 100

For a 1920×1080 input and --crop 1440x1080 --Halign 0, the window is 1440×1080 at x = 0: the right 480 pixels are removed. With --Halign 100, the window starts at x = 480 and the left 480 pixels are removed.

--Halign and --Valign accept any number between 0 and 100, and a trailing % is ignored (--Halign 25% equals --Halign 25).

If the requested window is wider or taller than the input, crop logs a warning and uses the original dimension for that axis.

If you pass --scale without --crop, crop only scales the video, and percentages in --scale refer to the original size.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Exact pixels
vexy-vid crop --crop 1280x720 --input video.mp4

# Aspect ratio, window at the bottom of the frame
vexy-vid crop --crop 16:9 --Halign 0 --Valign 100 --input video.mp4

# Half the width and half the height
vexy-vid crop --crop 50%x50% --input video.mp4

# Crop to 16:9, then scale to 1920x1080
vexy-vid crop --crop 16:9 --scale 1920x1080 --input video.mp4

docs.title: trim
docs.text:
Remove pixels from the edges, like CSS padding in reverse.

vexy-vid trim [--top N] [--right N] [--bottom N] [--left N] [--Letterbox] [--subtitles] --input FILE
Flag Short Default Meaning --input -i standard input Input video path. When missing, one line is read from standard input. --output -o generated Output video path. --top -t 0 Pixels (100) or percentage of the height (10%) to remove from the top. --right -r 0 Pixels or percentage of the width to remove from the right. --bottom -b 0 Pixels or percentage of the height to remove from the bottom. --left -l 0 Pixels or percentage of the width to remove from the left. --scale none none Size to scale to after trimming. Percentages refer to the trimmed size. --Letterbox -L False Detect and remove black bars at the top and bottom. --subtitles none False Detect and remove the subtitle band at the bottom. --quality -q 1 0 fast, 1 balanced, 2 quality. --verbose -v False Show debug logs and ffmpeg's info output.

docs.title: How manual and detected trims combine
docs.text:
--Letterbox sets the top and bottom trims. --subtitles sets the bottom trim. When you also pass --top or --bottom, trim uses the larger value on each edge, so a manual value never reduces a detected one.

For a 1080-pixel-tall input with 140-pixel bars and --Letterbox --bottom 200, the top trim is 140 and the bottom trim is max(200, 140) = 200.

Letterbox detection only affects the top and bottom edges. Use --left and --right for pillarbox bars.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Before encoding, trim checks the result:

  • If the trims leave a width or height of zero or less, or remove more than half of the width or height, trim stops with ValueError: Trim values too large or invalid.
  • If the aspect ratio changes by more than 30 %, trim logs a warning and continues.
  • If the detected subtitle band is taller than half of the content height, trim reduces it to 30 % of the content height and logs a warning.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Remove fixed amounts
vexy-vid trim --top 100 --bottom 50 --input video.mp4

# Remove 10% from each side
vexy-vid trim --left 10% --right 10% --input video.mp4

# Remove letterbox bars
vexy-vid trim --Letterbox --input video.mp4

# Remove the subtitle band, and at least 20 pixels from the bottom
vexy-vid trim --subtitles --bottom 20 --input video.mp4

# Remove bars, then scale
vexy-vid trim --Letterbox --scale 1920x1080 --input video.mp4

docs.title: Size formats
docs.text:
--crop (in crop) and --scale (in both commands) take a size specification. It is parsed by parse_size() in vexy_vid/utils.py.

Format Example Result for a 1920×1080 reference W:H 16:9 The largest 16:9 window that fits: 1920×1080 W:H 4:3 1440×1080 WxH 1280x720 1280×720 P%xP% 50%x50% 960×540 P% 50% 960×540 Wx 1280x 1280×1080 (height unchanged) xH x720 1920×720 (width unchanged) Mixed 1280x50% 1280×540

A ratio keeps one full dimension: if the target ratio is wider than the input, the full width is kept and the height is reduced; otherwise the full height is kept and the width is reduced. The x separator is not case-sensitive. Any other format raises ValueError: Unrecognized size format.

The edge flags of trim (--top, --right, --bottom, --left) take a single value: a pixel count or a percentage.

docs.title: Output file names
docs.text:
When you do not pass --output, the output goes next to the input as <name>_<command>_<parameters><extension>.

Command Output name vexy-vid crop --crop 16:9 -i movie.mp4 movie_crop_16-9.mp4 vexy-vid crop --crop 50%x50% -i movie.mp4 movie_crop_50px50p.mp4 vexy-vid trim --top 100 --bottom 50 -i movie.mp4 movie_trim_t100_b50.mp4 vexy-vid trim --Letterbox -i movie.mp4 movie_trim_llb.mp4 vexy-vid trim --subtitles -i movie.mp4 movie_trim_ssub.mp4

In crop names, : becomes - and % becomes p. In trim names, each parameter is written as its first letter followed by its value. An existing file with the same name is overwritten.

docs.title: Audio and container
docs.text: The audio stream is copied without re-encoding (-acodec copy). The output container follows the output file extension, because ffmpeg chooses the muxer from the file name.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: When an operation fails, the Python exception is printed with a traceback and vexy-vid exits with status 1.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: vexy-vid lives at github.com/vexyart/vexy-vid. Bug reports and pull requests are welcome.

docs.title: Set up a development environment
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Python 3.10 or newer, uv, git and ffmpeg.

  1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-vid.git
cd vexy-vid

  2. Create a virtual environment and install the package with the development extras:

    uv venv
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
pytest tests/

The suite has two kinds of tests:

  • Unit tests (test_utils.py, test_analysis.py, test_encoder.py, test_smoke.py) need no ffmpeg. They cover size parsing, output names, trim validation, the Numba kernels on synthetic frames and the encoder settings.
  • Integration tests (test_integration.py) build a 320×240 test clip with 40-pixel black bars using ffmpeg's testsrc and pad filters, then run crop, trim and letterbox detection on it end to end. The whole module is skipped when ffmpeg is not on PATH.

For a coverage report:

pytest tests/ --cov=vexy_vid --cov-report=term-missing

docs.title: Lint and format
docs.text:
The project uses ruff with a line length of 100 and a Python 3.10 target:

ruff check src/ tests/
ruff format src/ tests/

The pyproject.toml contains targeted ignores for the capitalised Halign, Valign and Letterbox parameters, which are part of the command-line interface.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text:
.github/workflows/ci.yml runs on every push and pull request to main. It installs ffmpeg, then runs ruff check, ruff format --check and pytest on Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12.

.github/workflows/docs.yml rebuilds this documentation site into docs/ when files under src_docs/ change on main.

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
The documentation source is in src_docs/md/, and the configuration is src_docs/mkdocs.yml. To build the site into docs/:

src_docs/build.sh

To preview it at http://127.0.0.1:8000 while you edit:

src_docs/build.sh serve

docs.title: Build the package
docs.text:
./build.sh package

This removes dist/, runs uv build and checks the result with twine check. ./build.sh with no argument builds the documentation and the package.

docs.title: Versioning and releases
docs.text:
The version comes from the git tag through hatch-vcs; there is no version number in pyproject.toml. During a build, hatch-vcs writes src/vexy_vid/_version.py, which is not tracked by git.

Maintainers release with ./publish.sh. It runs gitnextver to commit, tag the next vX.Y.Z version and push, then builds the package and uploads it with uv publish. Pushing a v* tag also triggers .github/workflows/release.yml, which builds the package, publishes it to PyPI with trusted publishing (skipping files that already exist) and creates a GitHub release.

docs.title: Automatic detection
docs.text: trim can measure two things on its own: the black letterbox bars at the top and bottom of the frame (--Letterbox), and the subtitle band near the bottom (--subtitles). Each has a primary method and a fallback.

docs.title: Primary method: ffmpeg cropdetect
docs.text:
vexy-vid runs ffmpeg with the cropdetect=24:16:0 filter over the first 60 seconds of the input and discards the decoded output:

ffmpeg -hide_banner -i movie.mp4 -t 60 -vf cropdetect=24:16:0 -f null - -loglevel info

cropdetect prints lines such as crop=640:352:0:64 while it runs. vexy-vid reads the last of these lines and turns it into trims:

  • top trim = the y offset (64)
  • bottom trim = input height − (y + detected height) = 480 − (64 + 352) = 64

Only the vertical values are used. The x offset and width are ignored, so pillarbox bars on the sides are not removed.

docs.title: Fallback: frame analysis
docs.text:
If cropdetect reports nothing usable, vexy-vid samples 10 frames spread evenly across the whole video and analyses each one:

  1. The frame is decoded with PyAV and downscaled to 640 pixels wide.
  2. It is converted to greyscale.
  3. The mean brightness of every row is computed.
  4. Rows are scanned from the top edge downward, through the top third of the frame, until a row's mean brightness is above 30 (on a 0–255 scale). The rows before it are the top bar.
  5. The same scan runs from the bottom edge upward through the bottom third.

The median top and bottom values across all sampled frames are scaled back to the original resolution and used as the trims. If no frame can be analysed, or both values are zero, trim logs No letterbox detected and continues without a letterbox trim.

docs.title: Primary method: shape analysis
docs.text:
vexy-vid samples 20 frames between 10 % and 90 % of the video, skipping the start and end where titles and credits often appear. For each frame:

  1. The frame is downscaled to 640 pixels wide.
  2. Only the bottom 30 % of the frame is kept.
  3. Pixels brighter than 200 become white; all others become black.
  4. The white areas are dilated with a 20×3 rectangle, twice, so that the letters of one line merge into one shape.
  5. Each shape's bounding box is tested. A shape counts as subtitle text if it is wider than 10 % of the frame, taller than 10 pixels, and less than half the height of the bottom region.
  6. The top edge of the highest qualifying shape is recorded.

The highest top edge across all frames is scaled to the original resolution. The bottom trim is the distance from that edge to the bottom of the frame, plus a 20-pixel margin.

docs.title: Fallback: brightness scan
docs.text: If the shape analysis finds nothing, vexy-vid samples 30 frames between 10 % and 90 % of the video and counts bright pixels (above 200) in each row of the bottom quarter. Rows with more than 50 bright pixels contribute to an average. The first row whose average is above 30 % of the maximum marks the top of the subtitle band; the bottom trim is computed from it with a 10-pixel margin.

docs.title: Safety limit
docs.text:
Subtitle detection can mistake bright scenery for text. If the detected band is taller than half of the content height (the height after letterbox trims), trim reduces the subtitle trim to 30 % of the content height and logs:

Subtitle trim adjusted to <N>px to preserve content

Tip

Detection works best on videos with white or light subtitles burned into the picture. For yellow or dark subtitles, or for a known fixed band, pass --bottom with an explicit value instead.

docs.title: The analysis cache
docs.text:
Every detection result is stored in a JSON file:

~/.cache/vidcrop/analysis_cache.json

Each entry is keyed by an MD5 hash of the file path, the file size and the modification time, plus the analysis type and sample count. A second --Letterbox or --subtitles run on an unchanged file reads the stored value and skips the analysis. Log lines such as Using cached letterbox detection result (visible with --verbose) show when this happens.

Editing or re-saving the file changes its size or modification time, so the next run analyses it again. To clear all stored results, delete the file:

rm ~/.cache/vidcrop/analysis_cache.json

docs.title: Tuning values
docs.text:
The thresholds live in src/vexy_vid/constants.py. They are not exposed as command-line flags.

Constant Value Used for BLACK_THRESHOLD 30 Row brightness below which a row counts as black SUBTITLE_BRIGHTNESS_THRESHOLD 200 Pixel brightness above which a pixel counts as text MORPH_KERNEL_WIDTH / MORPH_KERNEL_HEIGHT 20 / 3 Dilation rectangle that joins letters MIN_SUBTITLE_WIDTH_RATIO 0.1 Minimum text-shape width, as a fraction of the frame width MAX_SUBTITLE_HEIGHT_RATIO 0.5 Maximum text-shape height, as a fraction of the bottom region ANALYSIS_FRAME_WIDTH 640 Width that frames are downscaled to before analysis CACHE_DIR ~/.cache/vidcrop Location of the analysis cache

docs.title: Hardware acceleration
docs.text: vexy-vid encodes on the GPU when ffmpeg can. It does not assume that a GPU exists: it tests each encoder against your ffmpeg build and uses only the ones that work.

docs.title: How the encoder is chosen
docs.text:
The first time a vexy-vid process encodes, it tests each encoder in turn by asking ffmpeg to encode one 64×64 black frame with it. An encoder that finishes within 5 seconds with exit status 0 is available. The results are kept for the rest of the process.

Hardware encoders are tested in this priority order:

Priority Encoder Backend 1 hevc_nvenc NVIDIA NVENC (H.265) 2 h264_nvenc NVIDIA NVENC (H.264) 3 hevc_qsv Intel Quick Sync (H.265) 4 h264_qsv Intel Quick Sync (H.264) 5 hevc_amf AMD AMF (H.265) 6 h264_amf AMD AMF (H.264)

Then the software encoders: libx265, then libx264.

vexy-vid picks the first available encoder in this combined list. On a machine without a supported GPU encoder, that is libx265 if your ffmpeg has it, otherwise libx264. If no encoder passes the test, libx264 is used.

The log shows the result:

Detected 2 available encoders: ['libx265', 'libx264']...
Using encoder: libx265 (quality: balanced)

Apple VideoToolbox

The VideoToolbox encoders on macOS (h264_videotoolbox, hevc_videotoolbox) are not in the list. On a Mac, vexy-vid encodes with libx265 or libx264.

docs.title: Fallback when a hardware encode fails
docs.text:
If ffmpeg fails while encoding with a hardware encoder, vexy-vid logs the error and runs the same job again with libx264:

Hardware encoding failed with hevc_nvenc: ...
Falling back to software encoding...

If the software encode also fails, or if the failed encoder was already a software encoder, the error is raised and the command exits with status 1.

docs.title: Quality levels
docs.text:
--quality takes 0, 1 or 2. Each level maps to settings for each encoder family:

Encoder 0 fast 1 balanced (default) 2 quality hevc_nvenc, h264_nvenc preset=p1 tune=ll preset=p4 cq=20 preset=p7 cq=18 hevc_qsv, h264_qsv preset=veryfast global_quality=22 preset=medium global_quality=20 preset=slow global_quality=18 hevc_amf, h264_amf quality=speed rc=cqp qp_i=22 quality=balanced rc=cqp qp_i=20 quality=quality rc=cqp qp_i=18 libx265, libx264 preset=faster crf=22 preset=medium crf=20 preset=slow crf=18

Lower crf, cq, global_quality and qp_i values mean higher quality and larger files.

Levels 0 and 1 ask for a hardware encoder first. Level 2 asks for the first available encoder without that preference; because hardware encoders come first in the list, this is still a hardware encoder when one is available.

docs.title: The ffmpeg build decides
docs.text:
Which encoders are available depends on how your ffmpeg was compiled and on the drivers installed. A typical Homebrew ffmpeg on Apple Silicon has no NVENC, Quick Sync or AMF support, so vexy-vid uses libx265. That is expected.

To see which encoders your ffmpeg reports:

ffmpeg -hide_banner -encoders | grep -E 'nvenc|qsv|amf|libx26'

An encoder can appear in this list and still fail the test, for example when the GPU driver is missing. vexy-vid only uses encoders that pass the test.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: vexy-vid has two parts: the Python package, installed from PyPI, and the ffmpeg binary, installed with your operating system's package manager.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 or 3.13.
  • uv or pip.
  • Permission to install system packages (for ffmpeg).

docs.title: Install ffmpeg
docs.text:
ffmpeg does the encoding and the primary letterbox detection. It cannot be installed with pip.

macOSDebian / Ubuntu 
brew install ffmpeg

sudo apt install ffmpeg

Check that ffmpeg and ffprobe are on your PATH:

ffmpeg -version
ffprobe -version

vexy-vid calls both. It uses ffprobe (through ffmpeg-python) to read the video dimensions before every operation.

docs.title: Install vexy-vid
docs.text:
1. Install the package:

    uv pip install vexy-vid

    Or with pip:

    pip install vexy-vid

  2. Check that the command is available:

    vexy-vid --help

    The output lists the two commands, crop and trim.

To run it once without installing, use uvx:

uvx vexy-vid crop --help

docs.title: What gets installed
docs.text:
The package pulls in these Python dependencies automatically:

Package Role in vexy-vid fire Builds the command-line interface from the crop and trim function signatures. ffmpeg-python Builds and runs the ffmpeg encode command and calls ffprobe. av (PyAV) Extracts single frames for analysis. opencv-python Thresholding and morphology for subtitle detection. numpy Array maths for frame analysis. numba Compiles the per-pixel luminance and brightness loops. loguru Log output and --verbose mode. rich The status spinner shown while a video encodes. psutil Listed as a dependency.

numba compiles its functions the first time they run, so the first detection run can take a few extra seconds. The compiled code is cached by Numba for later runs.

docs.title: Development install
docs.text:
To work on vexy-vid itself, clone the repository and install it in editable mode with the development extras:

git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-vid.git
cd vexy-vid
uv venv
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

The dev extra adds pytest, pytest-cov and ruff. See Contributing for the test and lint commands.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page takes one file through the main operations. Each command writes a new file next to the input and leaves the input unchanged.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• vexy-vid and ffmpeg installed. See Installation.
  • A video file. The examples use movie.mp4, a 640×480 clip with 64-pixel black bars at the top and bottom.

docs.title: Remove letterbox bars
docs.text:
1. Run trim with --Letterbox:

    vexy-vid trim --Letterbox --input movie.mp4

  2. Read the log. vexy-vid reports what it found and what it will do:

    Detecting letterbox bars...
Detected letterbox crop: 640x352 at (0,64)
Letterbox detected via FFmpeg: top=64, bottom=64
Crop would significantly change aspect ratio: 1.33 -> 1.82
Trimming: top=64, right=0, bottom=64, left=0
Result dimensions: 640x352
Output: movie_trim_llb.mp4
Using encoder: libx265 (quality: balanced)

The result is movie_trim_llb.mp4, 640×352 pixels. The aspect-ratio warning is expected here: removing the bars changes the frame shape on purpose.

docs.title: Crop to an aspect ratio
docs.text:
1. Run crop with a ratio:

    vexy-vid crop --crop 16:9 --input movie.mp4

  2. vexy-vid keeps the full width (640) and computes the height for 16:9 (360). It centres the window vertically because --Valign defaults to 50.

The result is movie_crop_16-9.mp4, 640×360 pixels.

To keep the bottom of the frame instead of the middle, set --Valign 100:

vexy-vid crop --crop 16:9 --Valign 100 --input movie.mp4

docs.title: Trim fixed amounts
docs.text:
vexy-vid trim --top 100 --bottom 50 --input movie.mp4

This removes 100 pixels from the top and 50 from the bottom. The result is movie_trim_t100_b50.mp4, 640×330 pixels.

Use percentages for proportional trims:

vexy-vid trim --left 10% --right 10% --input movie.mp4

docs.title: Crop and scale in one pass
docs.text:
vexy-vid crop --crop 16:9 --scale 1920x1080 --input movie.mp4

vexy-vid crops to 16:9 first, then scales the cropped frame to 1920×1080. Both steps run in the same ffmpeg filter chain, so the video is encoded only once.

docs.title: Choose the output name
docs.text:
Pass --output to set the file name yourself:

vexy-vid trim --Letterbox --input movie.mp4 --output movie-clean.mp4

An existing file at that path is overwritten without a prompt.

docs.title: Pass the input path on standard input
docs.text:
When --input is missing, vexy-vid reads one line from standard input and uses it as the path:

echo movie.mp4 | vexy-vid crop --crop 50%x50%

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• CLI reference lists every flag and size format.
  • Automatic detection explains --Letterbox and --subtitles.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: vexy-vid reports problems as Python exceptions. The last line of the traceback names the problem. This page lists the common ones.

docs.title: ffprobe error (see stderr output for detail)
docs.text:
ffmpeg._run.Error: ffprobe error (see stderr output for detail)

vexy-vid reads the video dimensions with ffprobe before doing anything else. This error means ffprobe could not read the input. Check that:

  1. The path passed to --input exists and is spelled correctly.
  2. The file is a video that ffmpeg can open: ffprobe movie.mp4.
  3. ffprobe is on your PATH: ffprobe -version.

If ffprobe itself is missing, the error is FileNotFoundError instead. Install ffmpeg as described in Installation.

docs.title: ValueError: No input provided via stdin
docs.text:
You did not pass --input, so vexy-vid read a line from standard input and the line was empty. Pass the path with --input (or -i), or pipe it in:

echo movie.mp4 | vexy-vid trim --Letterbox

If you run vexy-vid crop in a terminal without --input and without a pipe, it waits for you to type a path and press Return.

docs.title: ValueError: Trim values too large or invalid
docs.text:
The requested trims would remove more than half of the width or height, or leave nothing at all. trim checks this before encoding. Reduce the values.

For example, --top 60% on its own removes 60 % of the height and fails. A combined --top 30% --bottom 30% also fails, because together they remove 60 %.

docs.title: ValueError: Unrecognized size format
docs.text: The value of --crop or --scale is not one of the supported formats. Use 16:9, 1280x720, 50%x50%, 50%, 1280x, x720 or a mix such as 1280x50%. See Size formats.

docs.title: No letterbox detected
docs.text:
Neither cropdetect nor the frame analysis found black bars. Possible reasons:

  • The bars are not black enough. The frame analysis treats rows with a mean brightness above 30 (out of 255) as picture.
  • The bars are on the sides (pillarbox). Letterbox detection only trims the top and bottom. Use --left and --right.
  • The first 60 seconds of the video differ from the rest, for example a full-frame intro. cropdetect only looks at the first 60 seconds.

Pass explicit values with --top and --bottom in these cases.

docs.title: No subtitles detected
docs.text: Subtitle detection looks for bright text (above 200 out of 255) in the bottom part of the frame. It does not find dark or coloured subtitles, and it cannot see soft subtitles stored as a separate stream. Use --bottom with a fixed value instead.

docs.title: A detection result looks wrong after the file changed
docs.text: Detection results are cached in ~/.cache/vidcrop/analysis_cache.json, keyed by path, size and modification time. If you replaced a file with another of the same size while keeping its modification time, the old result is reused. Delete the cache file to force a new analysis.

docs.title: objc[...]: Class AVFFrameReceiver is implemented in both ...
docs.text: On macOS, PyAV and opencv-python each ship their own copy of FFmpeg's libavdevice library, and the Objective-C runtime warns about the duplicate classes at start-up. The warning has had no functional effect in testing; the output is correct. It does not appear on Linux or Windows.

docs.title: The encode uses libx265 even though the machine has a GPU
docs.text: vexy-vid supports NVIDIA NVENC, Intel Quick Sync and AMD AMF only, and only when your ffmpeg build includes them and the encoder passes a test encode. Apple VideoToolbox is not supported. Run with --verbose to see which encoders were found. See Hardware acceleration.

docs.title: Getting more detail
docs.text:
Add --verbose to any command. It switches logging to debug level and raises ffmpeg's log level from error to info, so the encoder's own messages appear.

vexy-vid trim --Letterbox --input movie.mp4 --verbose

If the problem persists, open an issue at github.com/vexyart/vexy-vid/issues with the command, the full output, and the output of ffmpeg -version.
